from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Initialize Layout

        lines = [
            'This is the most beautiful formula in all mathematics.',
            'It unites five fundamental constants in one simple bridge.',
            'Meet zero, one, e, i, and pi.',
            'At first, they seem like complete strangers.',
            'Yet they form a single, perfect mathematical family.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Using unicode for pi

        i_sym = Text("i", color=WHITE)
        pi_sym = Text("π", color=WHITE)
        one_sym = Text("1", color=WHITE)
        zero_sym = Text("0", color=WHITE)
        
        plus_sym = Text("+", color=WHITE)
        equal_sym = Text("=", color=WHITE)
        
        # Bridge asset
        bridge_asset_path = "/mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg"
        bridge_icon = SVGMobject(bridge_asset_path).set_color("#ADD8E6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Five symbols appear at random grid positions
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.place_at_grid(e_sym, "A2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(i_sym, "B5", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_sym, "D1", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(one_sym, "E6", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(zero_sym, "F3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(e_sym), FadeIn(i_sym), FadeIn(pi_sym), 
            FadeIn(one_sym), FadeIn(zero_sym),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The symbols glide smoothly into a horizontal line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(
            e_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C1"]),
            i_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C2"]),
            pi_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C3"]),
            one_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C4"]),
            zero_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C5"]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in operators and form the formula e^{i pi} + 1 = 0
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Positioning for formula: e(C1), i(B2), pi(B3), +(C4), 1(C5), =(C6), 0 (manual offset from C6)
        # Note: B2/B3 are above C1/C2 to represent superscript
        
        self.place_at_grid(plus_sym, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(equal_sym, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            e_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C1"]).scale(1.0),
            i_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["B2"]).scale(0.7),
            pi_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]).scale(0.7),
            FadeIn(plus_sym),
            one_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C5"]).scale(1.0),
            FadeIn(equal_sym),
            zero_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C6"]).scale(1.0),
            run_time=2
        )
        # Adjusting the formula to look better within the 6 columns
        # e(C1), i(B1.5-ish), pi(B2), +(C3), 1(C4), =(C5), 0(C6)
        self.play(
            e_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C1"]),
            i_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["B2"]*0.7 + self.grid["C1"]*0.3 + UP*0.2), # Manual nudge for visual clarity
            pi_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["B2"]*1.2 + UP*0.2),
            plus_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C3"]),
            one_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C4"]),
            equal_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C5"]),
            zero_sym.animate.move_to(self.grid["C6"]),
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Strangers - draw bridge asset
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Place bridge icon in the area between e and 0
        self.place_in_area(bridge_icon, "A1", "B6", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bridge_icon, shift=UP), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Family - scale and change color to gold
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        formula_group = VGroup(e_sym, i_sym, pi_sym, plus_sym, one_sym, equal_sym, zero_sym)
        
        self.play(
            formula_group.animate.scale(1.2).set_color("#FFD700"),
            bridge_icon.animate.scale(1.1).set_color("#FFD700"),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Prerequisite 2: The Identity of 'e'"
        lines = [
            'The constant e is the base of natural growth.',
            'Usually, it drives scaling in a straight line.',
            'What happens if growth is pushed in imaginary directions?'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_E = "#FFA500"  # Orange
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"  # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_E))
        
        # Static Axes for reference
        real_axis = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D6"], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=2)
        imag_axis = Line(self.grid["F3"], self.grid["A3"], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=2)
        origin = self.grid["D3"]
        self.add(real_axis, imag_axis)

        # Constant 'e' label - Fixed: Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid latex dependency
        e_label = Text("e", color=COLOR_E, slant=ITALIC)
        self.place_at_grid(e_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        # Growth vector along real axis
        growth_vec = Arrow(origin, self.grid["D4"], color=COLOR_E, buff=0)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(e_label),
            GrowArrow(growth_vec)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight second line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_E)
        )
        
        # Scaling growth vector (straight line growth)
        new_vec_target = Arrow(origin, self.grid["D6"], color=COLOR_E, buff=0)
        self.play(Transform(growth_vec, new_vec_target))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight third line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        )

        # Update label to e^{ix} - Fixed: Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid latex dependency
        e_ix_label = Text("e^ix", color=COLOR_E, slant=ITALIC)
        self.place_at_grid(e_ix_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        # Vector bends upwards into imaginary plane
        # Reset vector to standard length first for clearer rotation visualization
        base_vec = Arrow(origin, self.grid["D4"], color=COLOR_E, buff=0)
        
        # Text "Pushing growth into the imaginary direction"
        push_text = Text("Pushing growth into the imaginary direction", font_size=24, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        self.place_in_area(push_text, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=0.7)

        self.play(
            Transform(e_label, e_ix_label),
            Transform(growth_vec, base_vec)
        )
        
        # Rotation animation
        self.play(
            Rotate(growth_vec, angle=PI/2, about_point=origin),
            Write(push_text),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Title and Layout
        # Replaced Title (which uses Tex) with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        title = Text("The Bridge of Beauty: Euler's Formula", font_size=36).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(title)

        # Left-side Bullet Points
        # Replaced Tex with Text and unicode bullet point
        bullet_points = VGroup(
            Text("• Unifying Exponential and Trig Functions", font_size=28),
            Text("• The Path in the Complex Plane", font_size=28),
            Text("• Magnitude is always 1", font_size=28),
            Text("• Angle is determined by x", font_size=28),
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        bullet_points.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5).shift(UP * 0.5)

        # 2. Complex Plane (Right Side)
        plane = ComplexPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        ).to_edge(RIGHT, buff=1)
        
        # Replaced get_axis_labels (which defaults to MathTex) with manual Text objects
        x_label = Text("Re", font_size=24).next_to(plane.x_axis.get_end(), RIGHT)
        y_label = Text("Im", font_size=24).next_to(plane.y_axis.get_top(), UP)
        labels = VGroup(x_label, y_label)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=plane.get_x_unit_size(), color=YELLOW).move_to(plane.get_origin())
        
        # 3. Dynamic Elements
        theta_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Moving Vector
        vector = always_redraw(lambda: Vector(
            plane.coords_to_point(
                np.cos(theta_tracker.get_value()), 
                np.sin(theta_tracker.get_value())
            ),
            color=BLUE
        ))
        
        # Formula Display - Replaced MathTex with Text
        formula = Text(
            "e^ix = cos(x) + i sin(x)", 
            font_size=42, 
            color=WHITE
        ).next_to(bullet_points, DOWN, buff=1.5).shift(RIGHT * 1.5)

        # 4. Animation Sequence
        self.play(
            Write(bullet_points),
            Create(plane),
            Write(labels),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(circle), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        
        # Animate the movement along the circle
        self.play(
            theta_tracker.animate.set_value(PI / 2),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        # Highlight a specific value (Euler's Identity component)
        target_point = Dot(plane.coords_to_point(-1, 0), color=RED)
        # Replaced MathTex with Text and unicode symbol
        identity_label = Text("e^iπ = -1", font_size=36, color=RED).next_to(target_point, DOWN)
        
        self.play(
            theta_tracker.animate.set_value(PI),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(target_point),
            Write(identity_label)
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

        # Cleanup
        self.play(
            FadeOut(bullet_points),
            FadeOut(plane),
            FadeOut(labels),
            FadeOut(circle),
            FadeOut(vector),
            FadeOut(formula),
            FadeOut(target_point),
            FadeOut(identity_label),
            FadeOut(title)
        )

    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout with script and title
        title_text = "The Half-Circle Journey (π)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "If we set x to pi, we travel halfway.",
            "This half-circle journey starts at positive one.",
            "After distance pi, we land exactly at negative one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Define custom colors
        GREEN_HIGHLIGHT = "#00FF00"
        RED_LANDING = "#FF0000"
        
        # Calculate the center of the visual area (grid A1-F6 center)
        # Center x: (0.5+5.5)/2 = 3.0; Center y: (2.2-2.8)/2 = -0.3
        center_point = np.array([3.0, -0.3, 0])
        
        # Setup Axes and Circle
        # We use a scale where 1 unit = 1.5 grid units
        # This makes the point (1,0) land at grid col 5 and (-1,0) at grid col 2
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1], 
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1], 
            x_length=4.5, 
            y_length=4.5,
            axis_config={"color": BLUE_D, "stroke_width": 2},
            tips=True
        )
        # Align axes to the visualization area
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        unit_circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=GRAY_D, stroke_width=2)
        unit_circle.move_to(center_point)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line: 'If we set x to pi, we travel halfway.'
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(
            Create(axes),

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line: 'This half-circle journey starts at positive one.'

            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)

        # Define start point at (1,0) in our coordinate system
        # Relative to center_point, (1,0) is center_point + 1.5*RIGHT
        start_dot = Dot(center_point + RIGHT * 1.5, color=WHITE)
        
        # Label "1" placed at grid C5 (approx 0.5 units above the point)
        label_one = Text("1", font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(label_one, "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(start_dot), Write(label_one))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line: 'After distance pi, we land exactly at negative one.'
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # The semi-circle path highlight (bright green)
        arc_highlight = Arc(
            radius=1.5, 
            start_angle=0, 
            angle=PI, 
            color=GREEN_HIGHLIGHT,
            arc_center=center_point,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        # The explorer dot representing our position
        explorer_dot = Dot(center_point + RIGHT * 1.5, color=WHITE, radius=0.12)
        
        # Large red "-1" text at landing spot (Grid C2)
        label_neg_one = Text("-1", font_size=48, color=RED_LANDING)
        self.place_at_grid(label_neg_one, "C2", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Transition from static start dot to moving explorer
        self.remove(start_dot)
        self.add(explorer_dot)
        
        # Animate the journey along the circle
        self.play(
            Create(arc_highlight),
            MoveAlongPath(explorer_dot, arc_highlight),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        
        # Reveal the result of the journey
        self.play(Write(label_neg_one))
        self.play(Indicate(label_neg_one, color=RED_LANDING))
        self.wait(2)
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture notes
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Bridge of Beauty: Euler's Formula", 
            ["- Complex Exponentials", "- Unit Circle Rotation", "- The Final Identity"]
        )
        
        # Display Euler's Formula in the grid
        # Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        euler_formula = Text("e^iπ + 1 = 0", font_size=42, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(euler_formula, "C3", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        # Add a unit circle representation
        plane = ComplexPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": BLUE_E,
                "stroke_width": 1,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.3
            }
        ).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(plane, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color=WHITE).move_to(plane.get_origin())
        dot = Dot(plane.n2p(1), color=RED)
        # Using Text for labels to avoid LaTeX dependency
        label = Text("1", font_size=24).next_to(dot, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Animations
        self.play(Write(self.title), FadeIn(self.lecture))
        self.play(Write(euler_formula))
        self.play(Create(plane), Create(circle))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), FadeIn(label))
        
        # Animate rotation to e^{i*pi}
        self.play(
            Rotate(dot, angle=PI, about_point=plane.get_origin()),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        
        # Using Text for updated labels
        new_label = Text("-1", font_size=24).next_to(dot, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(label, new_label))
        self.wait(2)

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Set background color
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        
        # Title at the top
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=20, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7).shift(UP * 0.5)

        # Define animation grid (6x6) on the right half of the screen
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        # Positioning values calibrated for 16:9 aspect ratio
        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Map j (0 to 5) to x-coordinates
                # Map i (0 to 5) to y-coordinates
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.9
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        if grid_pos in self.grid:
            mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        else:
            mobject.move_to(RIGHT * 3)  # Default fallback to right side center

outline.topic: The Bridge of Beauty: Unveiling Euler’s Formula
outline.target_audience: High school seniors and first-year university students

sections.title: The Grand Encounter
sections.content: Introduce the formula e^(iπ) + 1 = 0 as the 'most beautiful' in mathematics. Highlight the mystery of connecting five fundamental constants: 0, 1, e, i, and π. Use a cinematic visual of these five symbols floating in space, merging into a single bridge.
sections.example: Imagine five strangers (e, i, π, 1, 0) from different countries meeting at a party and discovering they are all part of the same family.

sections.title: Prerequisite 1: The Secret Power of 'i'
sections.content: Define 'i' not just as the square root of -1, but as a directional operator. In the complex plane, multiplying by 'i' represents a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation. Show a character standing on a 2D coordinate grid (The Complex Plane).
sections.example: A 'Math Explorer' character starts at '1' on the horizontal axis. When multiplied by 'i', they jump 90 degrees up to the vertical axis.

sections.title: Prerequisite 2: The Identity of 'e'
sections.content: Briefly recap 'e' as the base of natural growth. Explain that in the real world, e^x represents continuous scaling (growing bigger or smaller). Transition to the idea: what happens if the growth is pushed in an 'imaginary' direction?
sections.example: Think of 'e' as an engine. Usually, it drives a car forward (growth). But adding 'i' to the steering wheel forces the car to turn constantly.

sections.title: The Transformation: From Growth to Rotation
sections.content: Introduce Euler's General Formula: e^(ix) = cos(x) + i sin(x). Visually demonstrate that as 'x' increases, the point doesn't grow outward; it travels along the circumference of a unit circle. Animate a tracing point moving around the circle like a clock hand.
sections.example: Imagine a drone tethered to the center of a field. Instead of flying away (real exponent), it flies in a perfect circle because its 'imaginary' navigation system keeps pulling it sideways.

sections.title: The Half-Circle Journey (π)
sections.content: Substitute x with π. Since π represents 180 degrees (a half-circle) in radians, the point traveling along the circle must stop exactly halfway around. Show the point starting at (1, 0) and landing at (-1, 0).
sections.example: Our 'Math Explorer' walks along the circular path for a distance of π. They started at the 'Positive 1' gate, and after half a lap, they are standing at the 'Negative 1' gate.

sections.title: The Final Equation
sections.content: Conclude that e^(iπ) = -1. By adding 1 to both sides, we reach the identity e^(iπ) + 1 = 0. Summarize the logic: e (growth) + i (rotation) + π (half a circle) lands us at exactly -1.
sections.example: The 'Math Explorer' looks back at the path: A journey across the imaginary world leads them straight back to the most solid reality of negative one.

storyboard.title: The Grand Encounter
lecture_lines: This is the most beautiful formula in all mathematics.
It unites five fundamental constants in one simple bridge.
Meet zero, one, e, i, and pi.
At first, they seem like complete strangers.
Yet they form a single, perfect mathematical family.
animations: Five mathematical symbols (e, i, \pi, 1, 0) appear at random positions, color #FFFFFF.
The symbols glide smoothly into a horizontal line: e, i, \pi, 1, 0.
Symbols for exponentiation, addition, and equality (^, +, =) fade in to form the formula e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0.
An elegant arc, represented by a bridge [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg], draws from e to 0 in light blue (#ADD8E6).
The entire equation e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0 scales up and changes color to gold (#FFD700).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite 1: The Secret Power of 'i'
lecture_lines: Let's look at i beyond just a square root.
Multiplication by i acts as a ninety-degree turn.
It rotates numbers from horizontal to vertical.
animations: A 2D complex plane appears with a white dot at coordinate (1, 0) labeled '1'.
A vector from the origin to (1, 0) rotates 90 degrees counter-clockwise to (0, 1), turning cyan (#00FFFF).
The label at (0, 1) changes to 'i', and text '90° Rotation' appears nearby.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite 2: The Identity of 'e'
lecture_lines: The constant e is the base of natural growth.
Usually, it drives scaling in a straight line.
What happens if growth is pushed in imaginary directions?
animations: The letter 'e' in orange (#FFA500) is shown with a vector representing growth along the real axis.
The exponent 'i' is added (e^{ix}), and the growth vector starts to bend upwards into the imaginary plane.
The text 'Pushing growth into the imaginary direction' appears in white (#FFFFFF) below.

storyboard.title: The Transformation: From Growth to Rotation
lecture_lines: Euler’s formula transforms growth into circular rotation.
As x increases, we move along the unit circle.
The point travels like a clock's steady hand.
It never flies away, but orbits the center.
Imaginary growth pulls the path into a perfect ring.
animations: A unit circle is drawn on the complex plane with a faint grey line (#808080).
A point starts at (1, 0) and traces a path along the circle as x increases from 0 to 2\pi.
Dashed yellow lines (#FFFF00) project the point's position onto the x-axis (cos x) and y-axis (sin x).
The formula e^{ix} = \cos(x) + i\sin(x) is displayed at the top, with x values updating in real-time.
The point pulses at a specific angle to emphasize its position on the circle.

storyboard.title: The Half-Circle Journey (π)
lecture_lines: If we set x to pi, we travel halfway.
This half-circle journey starts at positive one.
After distance pi, we land exactly at negative one.
animations: The point on the unit circle moves from 0 to \pi radians, tracing a semi-circle.
The semi-circle path is highlighted in bright green (#00FF00).
The point stops at (-1, 0), and the value '-1' is displayed in large red text (#FF0000).

storyboard.title: The Final Equation
lecture_lines: Thus, e to the i-pi equals negative one.
Adding one brings the entire system to zero.
e to the i-pi plus one equals zero.
Growth, rotation, and cycles merge in harmony.
Five strangers are now one unified truth.
animations: The equation e^{i\pi} = -1 is shown in the center of the screen.
The term '-1' is moved to the left side, transforming into '+ 1', resulting in e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0.
Each of the five constants (e, i, \pi, 1, 0) is highlighted with a different vibrant color.
The background dims, and the formula glows intensely.
The title 'The Bridge of Beauty' fades in above the completed equation.
